#3634. Team Ninja Is Using AI For Quality Assurance, But Insists Creative Choices ‘Must Be Done By Humans’

Team Ninja is known, in part, for developing difficult games, but producers Kohei Shibata and Masakazu Hirayama emphasized during an interview with INVEN Global at GCON 2026 in South Korea that thereâs a key difference between difficult and unfair. The pair also spoke about how the Koei Tecmo subsidiary approaches the use of AI in games development, and an awkward compromise between implementing the technology for repetitive QA tasks, while arguing that “what matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands.”

Shibata and Hirayama are best known for their work as producers on the Nioh and Wo Long series respectively, two games that take the combat-driven difficulty of the iconic Ninja Gaiden franchise and transpose it onto the world of samurai and Chinese mythology. Before the topic of AI arose, the two discussed the crucial role of player interaction and movement in their games, beginning with the similarities between all three franchises and most notably their swordplay and the focus on timing your attacks and reading an opponentâs next move. According to both, this process of requiring a player to learn an enemyâs next move and counter is key to straddling the line between challenging and frustrating play.

âI consider Nioh to be samurai action,â explained Shibata. âSamurai combat involves stillness and movement. You stand firmly grounded, observing the opponent’s moves, and deliver a sharp strike the instant an opening appears.â Meanwhile, for Hirayama on Wo Long, that game was defined by âaggressive Chinese martial arts action,â where âattack and defense flow together seamlesslyâ and where âaggressively attacking is important, but defense must also lead directly into the next attack.â

The two go on to argue that it’s important to make a game that is polished in a way that reduces friction between a player’s action and consequence. If a person fails, it must be their fault, not the game’s. âI believe [the core essence of action games is] control responsiveness,â Shibata explained. âWhen a player presses a button, the character must move exactly as they intended. If you press a button and the character doesn’t react properly, it causes frustration. Conversely, if a slight input causes an exaggerated movement, it feels awkward. Therefore, responsiveness to input must be simple and intuitive, and the movement must be communicated rapidly.â

We have seen numerous studios speak out in recent times about where they will and wonât use AI. While some Japanese developers are embracing the technology, others are more cautious, either avoiding it entirely or insisting they only use the technology for optimizing their development framework while leaving creative choices to humans. The latter is the direction being taken by Capcom with its next generation of RE Engine, and appears to also be the choice being made by Team Ninja, who are already using AI for QA purposes.

As Shibata explained, âCurrently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows. If we can use AI to shorten task times, we can dedicate that saved time toward elevating the game’s overall quality. In that sense, using AI is beneficial. However, since it is still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions.” He continued,

What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future.

Where, if anywhere, is an acceptable use of AI is a topic that remains up for debate, but it appears many developers are settling into a space where it is used to handle repetitive tasks. The use of AI in QA actually predates the modern conversations of generative AI, and doesnât necessarily rely on the tech: Sony, for instance, has been experimenting with AI for many years to test games. Whether this is something audiences are willing to tolerate, or indeed is something that will further threaten jobs in the games industry, remains to be seen.

#3633. GTA 6 causes surge in UK physical game sales, despite there being no disc in the box

Grand Theft Auto 6 has had a huge effect on physical game sales in the UK, despite not actually containing a disc in the box.

NielsenIQ data shows that GTA 6 drove boxed software sales up an enormous 409 percent for the launch period ending 21st November, compared to the previous week, resulting in the biggest week for UK physical game sales since Christmas 2018.

GTA 6 alone accounted for £32m of the total £43m boxed software sales, apparently - around 74 percent, with 88 percent of its sales generated on day-one. But it's not a champion or record-breaker in this regard. In fact, GTA 6 places 17th in the all-time table of first-week boxed revenue, which is refreshingly humbling given the money-making records it's been breaking elsewhere. This is to do with the overwhelming shift towards buying games digitally, of course.

Nevertheless, Rockstar is well represented in the all-time list (which stretches back to 1995), because it's none other than GTA 5 that sits at the top, and GTA 4 at 11th.

But the GTA 6 effect is that of a rising tide, with console hardware sales rising 38 percent, to their highest level since 2025. Specifically, PS5 sales rose 46 percent and Xbox Series sales jumped a considerable 75 percent. And it's been a similar result in the US, where PS5 and Xbox Series sales have more than doubled.

Gaming accessory sales also got a boost, with PS5 controller sales up 355 percent, gaming headset sales up 94 percent, and - more nichely - gaming chair sales up 32 percent, which is apparently in line with the 40 percent increase they experienced around GTA 5.

"While the physical games market looks very different today compared with previous blockbuster launches, GTA 6 has still made a huge impact," said NielsenIQ's Dorian Bloch. "Back in 2008, boxed software accounted for half of all games retail revenue for the combined sectors of software, hardware, and gaming accessories, compared with 15 percent so far in 2026. This is a reflection of the market increasingly shifting towards digital downloads."

It's against this backdrop, of course, that Sony made its hugely controversial decision to wind down production of PlayStation game discs starting January 2028. This has led to boycotts and backlash and much angry sentiment towards the company, but Grand Theft Auto 6's enormous digital success is likely to be a hard example to ignore.

#3632. Metal Slug Is The Latest Game From SNK In Line For A Movie Adaptation

The Saudi Arabian investment group is struggling to turn a profit from its investment in renowned Japanese developer SNK, as the 48-year-old company faces heavy losses following lower than expected sales. However, it might have have found a new medium through which to claw back its cash: the movies. After all, SNK’s series likeÂ Fatal Fury, The King of Fighters and Metal Slug still hold cultural capital. Amidst Saudi Arabiaâs many other investments is new film studio The Arena, which has just announced Metal Slug as the latest property from the game studio to be in the works for a movie adaptation.

First reported by Variety, the studio announced that the adaptation of the side-scrolling military action platformer is going ahead, withÂ I Love My Dad director James Morosini attached to the project. An initial plot loosely based on the already thin narrative of theÂ Metal Slug series has also been revealed, centered on a misfit quartet of army recruits known as Marco Rossi, Tarma Roving, Eri Kasamoto and Fio Germi, as they stand up to General Morden to save the world from evil. Which seems about as coherent as a movie based on a game where soldiers fight aliens, yetis and zombies can get.

The Arena, originally revealed last year as Arena SNK Studios, is headed up by Erik Feig, a veteran producer who helped bring the likes of Twilight and La La Land to the screen. It was formed with backing from Saudi Arabiaâs Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and so far all of its projects bar one have been licensed from the SNK library. Currently in production is a webtoon called The Art of Fighting, and a TV series and movie based on Fatal Fury. It’s also working on a movie tied to Samurai Spirits, another SNK property. Their only non-SNK project is adapting a yet-to-be-released novel known as Kill Current.

Since its unveiling, the Arena’s only tangible output has been selling SNK fashion merchandise and running an Instagram account that seems to post about almost anything except its actual movies. Still, perhaps these movies and the occasional clothing merchandising drop are where investors hope to make back their money on buying SNK. Metal Slug at least has a concept lending itself to a more typical action blockbuster, but the question remains, with most of the studioâs IP resonating more with older audiences, can they turn these SNK IPs into something with mass appeal?

Blizzard's latest patch prevents Alterac Valley from being a glorified reputation farm.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Despite being set in the past, WoW: Forever is an attempt to capture the spirit of the old game by injecting it with new quirks that challenge new and returning players alike to approach it differently than any other version of the MMO. This is why familiar old dungeons can drop new loot, like an armor set that turns you into a snake.

Blizzard has said that its goal is to "unsolve" the game as best it can so players don't settle into the same routines they're used to. This is especially true for min-maxed strategies that threaten to suck the fun out of enjoying the game, or "the journey", as Blizzard likes to call it.

It's a lofty goal that can't be achieved without persistently fiddling with the knobs that encourage players to do one thing over another—which is the very thing that differentiates WoW: Forever from WoW Classic.

This week, Blizzard stepped in to fix a problem that was brewing in its 40-player MOBA-esque PvP mode Alterac Valley. Players were avoiding PvP altogether, turning it into a glorified reputation farm.

"We’ve seen that players in Alterac Valley were frequently completing the battleground without capturing the objectives, so we’ve made some adjustments to incentivize a focus on the objectives rather than rushing to kill the enemy faction’s general," community manager Kaivax wrote.

The patch basically broke a popular 'zerg' strategy where one side rushed to end the match as fast as possible by beefing up the NPC defenders that stood in their way. Blizzard shifted some of the reputation and honor you'd normally get from killing the generals to the other objectives so players are encouraged to engage with the whole mode.

But, as I've seen with changes like this in the past few weeks, many players are upset that they can't just spam it for the rewards, and that others have already reaped the benefits of the old strategy. There are people in Reddit threads doing the math to highlight how much efficiency has been lost (it doesn't seem like much) and questioning the point of doing Alterac Valley at all.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While I sympathize with not wanting to do something that feels like a chore, it's a far worse problem to have an entire part of the game flattened into an AFK farm. Alterac Valley is supposed to feel like a large-scale war where you look at a big map and choose what objectives are worth fighting over as you try to weaken the enemy forces. The loot you get from maxing out your reputation with the associated factions is meant to be a reward for putting in the effort to learn what it takes to win.

The whole pitch for WoW: Forever is that it's not going to ditch everything with a new expansion every few years. Numbers can be tweaked down the line if the reputation grind is too much of a slog, but the mode should be fun to play so it's not treated like a box to check off in your character's journey. An inert PvP mode ruins the spirit of the MMO far more than a slightly longer reputation grind does.

I think this is a good example of a healthy change that shows Blizzard is committed to protecting core parts of the experience from becoming a treadmill that nobody enjoys. WoW: Forever's strengths are the ways it encourages you to participate in systems that aren't there to fill progression bars. As Harvey said in his WoW: Forever review, "Forever is proof that old-school MMO design deserves a second chance," and that requires taking a stance on what the game is and isn't meant to be.

WWE moved away from Survivor Series’ traditional format of all multi-man matches in the mid 90s. I get where Vince McMahon and company were coming from. It’s harder to build when you have so many moving parts, and it was harder to get people to buy PPVs back in the day without world title matches. In an effort to get back to the spirit of Survivor Series, Triple H has used a men’s and women’s WarGames match the last few years to keep that 5 on 5 format, but the event doesn't have quite the same prestige it once did. This year, however, he also threw in an old school Survivor Series elimination match, and the build has been the best thing on WWE television in months.

Seriously, if you have not been watching the segments for the United States versus Mexico match over the past several weeks, you have missed out big time. Cody Rhodes was picked as captain of the United States team. He quickly added CM Punk, who promptly appointed himself as co-captain. Since then, they’ve been trying to fill out the roster, and it’s led to a nice showcase for team members LA Knight and Je’Von Evans, as well as a fun segment with proposed team member The Miz and maybe the best segment of the entire year with a 70-something year old Hacksaw Jim Duggan who joined the team and then promptly quit after seeing a highlight reel of their Mexican opponents. I cannot freaking wait for the match, especially after Seth Rollins was added to maximize the drama.

Fortunately, there are some other exciting matches to look forward to, as well. The men’s War Games will feature the Bloodline against the 946, the latter of whom feel like they’re building some real momentum and are an actual threat to win. The women’s War Games match hasn’t had quite the same build, but it still features some top talent and should be a good showcase for younger talent as well. Throw in a pretty compelling Women’s World Championship match with Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch, and the card is really pretty solid.

Before I get into what I think is going to happen in each match, you can check out how I’ve done on predictions. I’ve given my take ahead of every PLE since WrestleMania 38, and while I’m not going to main event WrestleMania with this win-loss record, I could be competing for a midcard championship. Here’s a quick snapshot of the bigger WWE PLEs this year, as well as the overall record…

With all due respect to Team Mexico and especially Penta who currently holds the Money In The Bank Briefcase, this match is lopsided on paper. Cody, CM Punk and Seth are three of the biggest stars in the entire company, and Rhdoes especially does not lose unless it’s in a very key spot or in service of building to something larger or very memorably at WrestleMania 39, both. This match, however, feels like it’s really building toward something larger. It feels like a Mega Powers explode situation.

There’s been so much talk about Cody Rhodes possibly turning heel after punting Randy Orton, but I think it’s more likely we’re going to see CM Punk turn on Cody, or potentially turn full heel, as he’s clearly irate about Rhodes adding his longtime enemy Seth Rollins to the team. At minimum, the story of this match is going to be about the simmering tension between Rhodes, Punk and Rollins. Now, does that mean they’re going to actually lose the match? Not necessarily.

They could fight amongst themselves and wind up with some shock eliminations, or they could fight through the tension and win, pushing the inevitable turn further down the road.

I feel like the long-term goal here is to move us into a feud with Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez. Rumors have swirled that Perez was originally slated to win Money In The Bank. She appeared in Morgan’s backstage segment with her this past Monday. Lynch has talked about how Judgment Day is holding her back. She’s clearly going to play a factor here in some way. It would be easy to say she’ll turn on Morgan and cost her the belt, but I don’t think that’s going to happen.

First, I don’t think there’s been enough teasing of a Judgment Day break-up. Fans have speculated about it forever, but we haven’t gotten nearly enough friction since Finn left to maximize the possible payoff here. Doing it now would be underbaked and stupid. Second, I think what Roxanne actually wants is a shot at the title, and she’s going to ruin that if Morgan loses the title. So, I think she’s going to help her ensure Liv keeps it.

Throw in the fact that Liv is already committed to the John Cena classic, and I feel pretty confident she’s going to hold onto the belt here.

For the longest time, I was sure we were headed toward an Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair break-up, but curiously, WWE really hasn’t teased much friction between the two lately, not since Tatum Paxley's early main roster promotion. Without that dynamic, this really just feels like a run of the mill babyfaces vs heels match that we would get at a house show.

Maybe there’s an angle I’m not seeing here or one that will emerge during the show, but absent that, I’m going to pick the babyfaces because when in doubt, always pick the babyfaces. That’s just a standard wrestling rule, and given I think there’s a potential for a lot of heels to win on this card, it makes even more sense to go with the babyfaces.

Predicted Winner: Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley.

This is the moment where we find out how WWE really feels about 946 and Royce Keys. They’ve been the primary antagonists on the show for months and have been presented like really dangerous and unhinged monsters we should take seriously. If they lose here, it kind of feels like that’s the end. I mean I’m not saying they’re going to get released, but it feels like that’s the end of the audience taking them seriously. They’re the ones stepping up and trying to prove they’re main event players. If they lose in their first big PLE match trying to do that, then that tells the audience all they need to know.

I think WWE believes in them more than that. I think they also believe in the recently added Cruz Montana, and I think they see the 946 as another chance to push Carmelo. They really need this win in a way the Bloodline doesn’t, and if they do win, it would make all the sense in the world to build toward Keys getting a legit title shot at Royal Rumble against Roman Reigns. He would be a big underdog in that match, but he would at least be coming off some momentum from a victory here.

I think the 946 really needs to win, but WWE also almost never has the Bloodline actually lose. So, do I feel confident about this? No.

#3629. Nioh and Ninja Gaiden studio is using AI for QA, but argues "that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands"

Team Ninja (Nioh, Ninja Gaiden) is the latest game development studio to implement AI into some of its workflow, but producer Kohei Shibata still believes that fun games need to be "crafted by human hands."

The producer best known for the tough-as-nails Nioh trilogy and Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty spoke about the controversial tech during South Korea's GCON 2026, in an interview with INVEN Global. "Currently, we utilize AI in QA and various verification tasks to streamline certain workflows," Shibata explained.

He went on to argue that if AI can "shorten task times," then developers can spend more hours "elevating the game's overall quality" in other ways. "In that sense, using AI is beneficial." Team Ninja isn't fully on board with enforcing the tech elsewhere, though: "Since it's still a new technology, we are continuously evaluating the most appropriate ways to implement it. I imagine other game companies are facing similar questions." (Good spot, Kotaku.)

"What matters fundamentally is that a game becomes fun when crafted by human hands. Repetitive, simple tasks that anyone must perform can be streamlined using technology. But ultimately, deciding how to craft the game and what makes it enjoyable must be done by humans. Using AI itself should never become the goal. I believe the principle that humans must think for themselves and finish the game will remain unchanged in the future," Shibata continued.

Generative AI's use in game development is still a hotly debated topic among both players and the people making games, but it's been prevalent nonetheless. A recent report estimated that around 40 percent of game developers were using AI in some fashion, even if lots of them also agreed the tech was harmful. Bigger publishers like Ubisoft and Epic Games are more aggressively pursuing an AI-first future, too.

Team Ninja seems to be settling into a middle ground, at least, according to Shibata's statement. Speaking on the studio's approach to difficult games, he said that a player's failure should never be the game's fault. Dying in a game like Ninja Gaiden or Nioh should always be the result of human error, otherwise death "causes frustration." Finding that perfect, often bloody sweet spot is something only humans can do.

Microsoft-owned developer platform Github stepped in it earlier today when it posted a message on X celebrating the success of AnyPS5, an open source project that aims to let users port PS5 executables to PC, and then linked that success directly to efforts to port Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC. The message was deleted shortly after it was posted, but not before it was widely noticed and called out for being a very bad idea.

"GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on Github," the message stated (via Kotaku).

"The repo AnyPS5 has passed 58K stars since its August launch, rewriting PS5 executables to run on Windows and Linux. Does changing where games run cross a legal line? Share your take. Happy GTA VImas!"

Lest there be any misunderstanding, a video that accompanied the post made the GTA 6 connection explicit: "The project rewrites a game's executable so Windows and Linux can run it directly. Performance seems to be the main issue for users wanting to run GTA 6, with one contributor telling the project's community to 'lock in and get your agents to help' if they need to."

And here's the accompanying video from @github's GTA6 tweet https://t.co/crU9cpOWcsNovember 26, 2026

The question of whether or not this sort of thing crosses a legal line has, predictably, sparked debate among those who think they have a clear understanding of the answer. What caught most by surprise, though, is that Github—which is owned by Microsoft—would put forth the question in the first place, implicitly suggesting that it might not. GTA 6 publisher Take-Two Interactive has been pretty aggressive with its efforts to keep recompiled versions of GTA 6 from landing on PC, and I can't imagine it would too thrilled with Github—which, I must emphasize, is owned by Microsoft—telling the world that it might actually be okay to go ahead and vibe-code it up.

That point wasn't missed by redditors, one of whom described it as Github "openly taunting Sony and Rockstar." Even the AnyPS5 subreddit seemed baffled: Redditor superkickstart asked, "Do they have AI running their socials? Lol"

There's also a little bit of irony in the fact that, until earlier this week, the leading effort to get GTA 6 running on PC was based on an Xbox build of the game posted by GTA 6 leaker Cyberleeks. Beyond that, there are also some very obvious questions about how Github (owned by Microsoft) would react to AI-powered ports of, say, other software:

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The whole thing is weird, really, because it seems like such an obviously bad idea. The only explanation I can come up with is that a social media manager either didn't think about it, didn't understand it (which would be weird in itself for someone doing social media posts for Github), or just had a big ol' brain fart. Whatever the reason, I imagine someone got a good old-fashioned talking-to about it.

I've reached out to Github and Take-Two for comment and will update if I receive a reply.

#3626. The Witcher 3's new patch adds 40 cross-platform mods, fixes plenty of game-breaking bugs and "various lighting issues"

"The Path never sleeps, and the work is never done."

Developer CD Projekt Red has rolled out a new patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered on all platforms, which squashes dozens of bugs and adds 40 cross-platform mods with "more on the way."

"Two things are certain in a witcher's life: the Path never sleeps, and the work is never done," the studio wrote in its latest exhaustive list of patch notes for the decade-old game.

Patch 5.02's handiest changes come from those aforementioned bug fixes, many of which once caused the game to crash entirely or simply not work as intended. One such bug caused "time to go backwards indefinitely." Another turned Geralt bald. Opening the game with outdated mods could also result in a crash on PC. All of those, plus plenty more, have been fixed.

When The Witcher 3 Remastered first dropped, many players also took issue with the game's updated and sometimes "lifeless" lighting. Previous CDPR patches already targeted the lighting changes in question, but this newest patch continues to fix "various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes."

The studio specifically names "overly bright or dark areas" and "inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering."

The Witcher 3's free remastered upgrade also gave all console owners access to mod support, though not all pre-existing PC mods were available to download for console folks. This patch is expanding the selection somewhat with 40 new cross-platform mods, including glowy eyes for Geralt and a new monster hunt - and on social media, the studio promised "more on the way."

CD Projekt Red is still hard at work on two big upcoming sequels, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2. Speaking on the former in a recent earnings call, joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski said we can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as we've just seen from GTA 5 to GTA 6.

#3625. 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

This series will help you pick the perfect presents, decor, and activities to make this Christmas the Best Christmas Ever.

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

You can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

If Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting new movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:

Go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you plan to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

Dawn of War 4 writer John French lays out how it works.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The original Dawn of War's Winter Assault expansion added campaigns that let you play two factions at once, with different final missions based on which one you triumphed with. Dawn of War 2's campaign was even more player-led, with distress calls that had different outcomes based on what you prioritized and, in the Chaos Rising expansion, a morality mechanic with Corruption and Redemption points. It even chose a different character to be a traitor based on who gained the most Corruption by the story's end.

I asked John French, Dawn of War 4's writer and a Warhammer novelist, whether Dawn of War 4 would follow this noble tradition by having player decisions alter the plot. "The player's decisions very much change the perspectives that they'll experience the game from," he replied. "So, depending on which heroes from each faction they choose, they'll have a very different experience of the game, in that they'll see different parts of the story and sometimes different views on the same events."

Based on what we've seen of the Ork and Adeptus Mechanicus campaigns, that means partway through you'll be presented with a choice between two Commanders who have opposed goals and the one you pick will lead to missions with different objectives. Ork Beastboss Guzcutta is trying to unite his clan, the Snakebites, while his rival warboss, Gorgutz, is an off-world interloper trying to rebuild his damaged invasion force.

"With characters like Gorgutz and Guzcutta," French explained, "it can be as simple as one of them wants to do it the traditional, brutal ork way, and one of them wants to do it in a brutal but cunning way, so you have missions that focus on getting lots of shiny kit in one, while the other tries to get as many orks to follow them as possible.

"In a more complex narrative, like the Adeptus Mechanicus campaign, Potentia-Delta-9's main drive is the quest for knowledge, and she is on a very different path from Skitarii Marshal Sek-Ix-23, who is very much about enforcing the orthodoxy. The story for both overlaps, but which character you choose and what decisions you make with them lead down different experiences of an overlapping story."

Writing an RTS isn't all about plotting out the campaign missions. The Dawn of War games are legendary for their unit barks, like the saber-rattling Lord Commissar who shouts, from the top of an armored Chimera transport, "Drive me closer, I want to hit them with my sword!" Getting across so much personality in a short space is a real skill.

"You can do an awful lot with just a couple of words like 'More dakka!'," French said, "that tells you a huge amount about the orks on its own. Even with factions like the necrons, the way that the lower ranks respond to the higher ones with just 'Obedience,' one word, tells how their faction works."

Part of the appeal of Warhammer is the berserk variety of its armies, each with its own highly thematic identity. You walk into a shop and see the stoic space marines alongside spiky Chaos daemons and units of Astra Militarum who look like they stepped out of a trench in World War I before being given laser rifles.

"Dawn of War 4 is deeply Warhammer in that way because it's got all of these different textures of factions and characters next to each other," French said. "You have orks, and they are absolutely fixated on smashing everything they can in the pursuit of trying to have an even bigger fight. Then you've got the Adeptus Mechanicus, who revere machines as holy and worship the machine as god with complete sincerity and total conviction. Those two things literally exist side by side, along with alien races who have made themselves immortal by creating metal bodies with hyper advanced technology. And all of these different types of character come into conflict on one planet cut off in a sea of night—that's very Warhammer."

Dawn of War 4 is due out on December 3 and will be available on Steam. Owners of the Commander Edition will get advance access and can play from November 30.

Jody's first computer was a Commodore 64, so he remembers having to use a code wheel to play Pool of Radiance. He's written for Rock Paper Shotgun, The Big Issue, GamesRadar, Zam, Glixel, Five Out of Ten Magazine, and Playboy.com, whose cheques with the bunny logo made for fun conversations at the bank. Jody's first article for PC Gamer was about the audio of Alien Isolation, published in 2015. Jody edited PC Gamer Indie from 2017 to 2018, and he eventually lived up to his promise to play every Warhammer videogame.

#3622. EA removes some live service fluff from Skate and ends seasonal structure "in favour of regular, agile content updates"

EA is ditching seasonal updates and shaving some of the live service fluff off Skate (for some reason stylised as skate.) going forward. Normally, such news would be cause for concern. Here, the publisher assured players the transition will lead to more regular updates since devs can now push out new features without waiting for the next season to roll around.

"EA and Full Circle are committed to keep driving skate. forward. Just as a reminder, we're still very much in Early Access," the studio wrote in a new blog post. "The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game - especially when it comes to social features and progression. Ultimately, we want to build skate. in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet."

Skate's fifth and final season is coming to an end on 1st December, with Full Circle embracing a different model from there on out. "We are transitioning away from the traditional seasonal cadence in favor of regular, agile content updates," it explained.

Full Circle is also throwing out the skating sim's version of a seasonal battle pass (horribly named skate.Pass) by the end of the year, and will rethink how the game's progression system works: "We've said it many times: we have a long-term future vision for skate, and this is a key part of it. Update 0.33.1 will be our very first update in this post-season era."

The move away from rigid seasonal updates "gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle," the blog post continued. "This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We've started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process."

Full Circle's live service rejig also means the in-game currency Tix is being retired, and some maps will no longer be locked behind paywalls. Skate still has real-money microtransactions and a cosmetics store, though it's nice to see some of the more aggressive live service bits being plucked out.

The Nathan Fielder/Lance Oppenheim co-directed hit documentary You Can See Everything, which has done huge box office numbers on the 2026 movie schedule, does a very deep dive into Elizabeth Holmes after Theranos. Now, everyone from former employees to psychologists is weighing in on Holmes both before and after her fraud convictions led to a long prison sentence that she is currently serving in Texas. Recently, one of Holmes’ assistants, Aria Marinelli, from the early days of Theranos, appeared on the Assistants vs. Agents podcast and spoke about a few red flags she saw in her short time working for the disgraced CEO.

Marinelli worked for Holmes at Theranos in 2009, which lands right in the middle of the company’s history, which was founded in 2003 and collapsed in 2016 before going completely out of business in 2018. Holmes went to prison in 2023. Marinelli wasn’t at the company long, by the sound of things, but did work directly for Holmes in her time with the Silicon Valley startup that promised big things with what we now know was a completely fraudulent blood-testing machine (a machine Marinelli says she never even laid eyes on until seeing You Can See Everything).

In the interview, she highlights a few things that made her question whether she wanted to be part of the company and if what they were doing was legitimate. According to Marinelli, the suspicions started even before she accepted the job, as she explained:

I went and looked through old emails just to see if I was remembering correctly, and it turns out I was. So this is [an email to] a mentor of mine. I said: ‘It's looking like I have to get Theranos an answer tomorrow regarding their offer. It expires at COB, and they've already extended it once. I'm very hesitant to accept because the work and the work environment are really not my ideal next step. Something about it doesn't sit right, I guess.’

She went on to explain that pretty early on, there was never a lot of talk about what the company was trying to do with the machine. In typical Silicon Valley style, according to Marinelli, most of the talk was about stock shares, IPOs, and how much money they could all make. That was something else that didn’t sit right with her.

Not only did Marinelli never see the now-infamous device, but she never saw a blood testing lab at all and was worried that despite famous names on the board of directors, there seemed to be no one with medical knowledge. That also raised concerns for her, as she explained:

The biggest thing was that there was no lab. So I had noticed that there were no doctors on the board, and that's, again, been talked about ad nauseam, but I was willing to dismiss that as maybe they were just getting started, right? And I remember just being told, ‘Oh, it's off-site,’ but I never saw anybody in that time frame that was working in a lab or that was from that lab.

The final straw for Marinelli was when she was tasked with tracking down one of the company’s machines from the Army, which was supposedly testing it. Through multiple emails and phone calls, she seemed to be a wild goose chase, with everyone pointing to other people, and no one knowing where the device actually was. Marinelli told host Warner Bailey:

Everyone [at Theranos] is very secretive, very, you know, shielded in how they're speaking about this thing. I doubt they would just ship it off to someone and not have them have a concerted program around testing it.  So that, to me, was kind of the last flag that I was willing to put up with.

Marinelli also gave her honest impression of Holmes, and it wasn’t all negative, but she did mention that she thought The Dropout, the series starring Amanda Seyfried that can be seen with a Hulu subscription, is a fair portrayal of Holmes as Marinelli knew her. She also praised You Can See Everything and seems to have real sympathy for Holmes, saying, “everyone has to lie at that level.”

One of the many interesting and brilliant things about You Can See Everything is that everyone sees something different in it, including the people who worked for Holmes and Theranos, and I don’t think this is the last time we’ll hear from people who worked with her and knew her. Especially as this movie continues to get Oscar buzz and will continue to be in the cultural zeitgeist for some time.

#3620. Union Vote Fails In Landslide At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games As 75 Percent Of Devs Vote No

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Rockstar GamesUnion

Rockstar Games will not be forced to formally recognize a union at the Grand Theft Auto 6 studio after its developers based in the UK voted overwhelmingly against the initiative. The weeks-long voting process played out as Rockstar launched the open-world hit to over 30 million sales in its first day.

Voting began on November 12 and concluded today on November 26. Workers at Rockstar Games voted 75 percent against the recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The initiate would have formalized collective bargaining efforts around things like overtime, bonuses, layoffs, and AI. Developers in favor of unionizing can still work with the IGWB, but there will be no regular meetings with management to hash out new policies.

“We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6,” Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe said in a statement shared with Kotaku. “This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together.â

The IWGB Game Workers Union pushing the vote released the following statement:

For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isnât a sign to retreat, itâs a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. Weâre ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

Whilst we havenât emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.

A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But itâs one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. Weâll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.

The vote comes roughly a year after Rockstar fired dozens of developers it accused of gross misconduct and breaking confidentiality rules around the development of GTA 6. The fired workers accused the studio of union busting, which it has denied, and a legal fight has been ongoing over the last 12 months at a labor tribunal. A final judgement in that case is still pending. As recently as this month, members of both sides of the dispute were testifying on the record for the case.

Grinding Gear Games' Jonathan Rogers urges devs to lead with their best stuff.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Every few months, Grinding Gear Games resurfaces with livestreams to showcase all the new toys in the latest updates for Path of Exile 1 and 2. They play out quite differently from your usual game announcements, cutting straight to showing new gameplay features ahead of any preamble.

According to Path of Exile co-game director Jonathan Rogers, this is a key part of Path of Exile's success over the last 13 years. Speaking at games industry conference DevGAMM FTW!, he explained how GGG came up with a winning formula for PoE's seasonal update schedule.

The announcement streams aren't just marketing, he explained, they help dictate what kinds of things the team should focus on with every update. If it doesn't sound exciting enough to rally players around a new league, it doesn't get made.

After a teaser trailer reveals the theme and title of the league a few weeks before the full announcement, the stream dives right into the juiciest details—an approach that Rogers believes is paramount when it comes to selling the update.

Rogers says he's seen some "truly terrible livestreams for game announcements," before slipping in a quick jab: "Blizzard I'm looking at you."

I've watched enough Diablo 4 new season streams to know exactly what he's talking about even if I don't quite agree that it's strictly a bad way to do it. Blizzard typically likes to lead with some introductions before having individual developers break down what's coming in an update.

Admittedly, these can drag on for too long, especially if you don't particularly care about percentage changes to some item or stat. But I appreciate hearing the thought process behind each decision from the people responsible for that aspect of the game. In a time when certain very vocal segments of the audience prefer to think of studios as machines, it's a good way to remind people that real human beings are behind it all.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

That said, I think Rogers' specific point about too many studios wasting everyone's time by holding the best announcements for last is often true. For something like a new update to an ongoing game, everyone is watching to find out why this one is worth logging back in for. I want to see the standout details so I don't feel like I wasted 45 minutes for something I'm not that into.

Sometimes I do like the build-up and eventual payoff for a big reveal, though, like the way Blizzard dropped Diablo 5 at the end of the Diablo portion of this year's BlizzCon or how Larian surprised everyone with Divinity last year. Certain games earn the theatrics. If anything, Rogers' approach just underlines how important it is for studios to read the room and craft their announcements around the things that will actually spark interest rather than putting everyone to sleep.

I'm a hardcore reality TV fan, and this year is my first time watching a full season of The Great British Baking Show with my Netflix subscription. There was just one big problem: the heat wave in the U.K. was making it especially hot in the iconic tent. I thought this was going to be a big problem over the course of the season, and I feel totally vindicated after watching the semifinal episode of the season.

Can't we get some better air conditioning in the Bake Off tent?

#3616. 10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

You can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

If you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

While driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

Well, uh, Iâd wager that the publishers of Grand Theft Auto 6, Take-Two, would probably say that the answer to that question is a firm âYes,â considering that its been actively shooting down all of the GitHub repositories attempting to vibe-code a PC port of GTA 6 over the past week.

It’s probably pretty obvious why they opted to delete the post, but I can’t help but wonder what compelled GitHub’s social media team to ask the question in the first place.

Though Vermintide 2's had a Steam Workshop since 2018, it's mostly used for quality-of-life stuff like UI tweaks. That's set to change now that Fatshark has announced a public release of its internal developer tools, which they say "will allow modders to work their magic on both editing and creating anything from custom levels, models, textures, particles, animations, and more!"

Right now, only a select number of sanctioned mods can be used in Vermintide 2's "official realm" which is the one with loot and leveling that carries over, while unsanctioned mods can only be accessed in a "modded realm" where there are no progression systems. Obviously that's off-putting to a lot of players, so Fatshark has announced a change.

"We have an update releasing in early December which will see the Modded Realm have its own, local, offline progression. That means that playing in the Modded Realm will still result in you gaining loot and experience, but said progression will not reflect on the Official Realm. This should make playing on the Modded Realm feel much better and not be discouraging for those that want to try out all of the unsanctioned mods, both the ones that already exist and the ones to come thanks to the Mod Tools!"

I'm not sure how many players will be happy to start over from level one just to get access to a wider variety of mods, but I hope it encourages some folks to check them out. Another thing that'll encourage new players is that XP has been doubled from now through till Monday, and Vermintide 2 is on sale for 90% off on Steam. The DLC has been discounted too.

In less good news, the servers for Versus Mode are being turned off. "We have monitored the use of the dedicated Versus servers lately," Fatshark said, "and come to the conclusion that they are barely used. We have therefore decided to shut these down." Versus Mode will still be playable, but via the menu option for a custom game or the lobby browser. You'll have to find a crew to play with on Discord first, which is how everyone seems to play Versus at the moment anyway.

That shutdown is planned for early December, at the same time as the update that adds local progression to the modded realm. That update will also include balance changes to buff some unpopular talents, new weapon icons, and a Tome of Triumphs in the hub area that will point you at any event if there's a live one, or to the weekly event mode if there isn't. The next event planned is the annual return of Gifts of the Wolf Father in December.

Finally, Fatshark mentioned that focusing on the mod tools to get them ready for public release had to take priority from other updates. "The weapon pack and the level that we mentioned in the past has been put on hold," they wrote. "We still want to get back to that, especially the weapon pack, but for now there is no active development on that. It’s important for us that we have transparency here, and while we are not working on these things, we do stick with our games! We have plans both near and far for Vermintide 2."

For months, some fan favorites and newcomers alike at Warner Bros., New Line, Weta and even Hobbiton have been prepping for a brand new Lord of the Rings movie. Lips have been pretty tightly sealed about the new Hunt for Gollum project beyond the fact it’s set during the time shortly before the Fellowship of the Ring and will feature Andy Serkis both as director and Gollum himself. Returning cast members include Ian McKellen, Lee Pace and Elijah Wood stepping back into those Hobbit feet. Oh, and Jamie Dornan and Leo Woodall will provide some additional eye candy. (And good acting too, credit where credit is due!)

It’s hard to believe The Lord of The Rings: The Hunt For Gollum has already wrapped. The movie picked up principle photography in July of this year, and has been quietly chugging along for months, but it still feels like yesterday it was getting off the ground. This morning, Andy Serkis and co. revealed the movie has wrapped in a new post that has me champing at the bit to see what’s next.

The news comes just a few weeks after Jamie Dornan admitted he’d wrapped his own portion of the movie. (There may have been some crying involved.) For his part, Andy Serkis has shared his return in the mo-cap suit, and now we've gotten a taste at Gollum's return in this funny wrap video.

To note, I’m not the only one impressed by Serkis donning the mo-cap suit at 62, either.

Warner Bros. revealed the new franchise film will be returning to the Shire back in September, a fact I can also confirm thanks to a lovely visit to the set of the movie and Hobbiton, courtesy of the studio. The movie shot for several days on location in the real-life version of the Shire on the Alexander Farm before heading to the soundstage in New Zealand, and the end result should be nothing short of epic, but that will also mean there’s plenty to do in post ahead. The movie itself isn’t scheduled to hit theaters for over a year, but I’ll take any tidbit I can get in the meantime.

It’s been a great holiday season for Lord of the Rings fans already. Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power dropped its final two episodes for Season 3 this week, and Season 4 was announced! Now, we know the upcoming 2027 movie release is ready to go into post-production. It's a big week, but December 17th, 2027 couldn’t come soon enough.

#3612. AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

#3611. 12 Best Video Game Stocking Stuffers Under $30 That People Actually Want

Ugh. It’s my least-favorite time of year: Black Friday season. I hate this overwhelming capitalist-ass shopping holiday for many reasons, but one of my more petty pet peeves is the big push for the blandest, most cringey “gamer”-themed gifts ever at mainstream shopping destinations. I’m talking like, this “Smells like video game rage” candle, neon lights and blankets that say stuff like, “Can’t hear you, I’m gaming,” or the classic “I paused my game to be here” T-shirt. Crap that really leans into the awful “gamer” stereotype and that, for many of us, is embarrassing to receive from a relative who knows, like, one fact about us, which is that we are into video games.

If you’ve arrived at this article and have been guilty of giving such gifts before, please absolve yourself. The internet does not make this easy. Gaming gift guides are full of this junk, and if you’re not into games yourself, finding decent stuff for someone who likes them can be really annoying and challenging, especially on a budget. Most gamers probably have a lot of the tech and games they want already, and knowing what people have and what they might like can be extremely challenging if you don’t have an easy way to look at their Steam libraries.

So I’m here to give you a hand with 12 ideas for stocking stuffer gifts (read: will reasonably fit in a normal-sized Christmas stocking) under $30 that will probably be relevant to folks who like playing video games on the regular. These are all things that most people will be at least mildly pleased to receive and will probably use as long as you put in the bare minimum amount of thought to make sure you’re not getting Switch accessories for someone who doesn’t have a Switch or something.

Good controllers are so dang expensive and cheap ones are usually garbage, but the 8BitDo controllers are both of solid quality and inexpensive. These pleasant wireless controllers come in several cute pastel colors, are usable for PC gaming (or Android, I guess), and are quite inexpensive for as good as they are. Normally $29.99 on Amazon, as I write this they’re on sale for $22.99.

If you’ve got an Xbox gamer in the house, this charging stand works with all Xbox Series, One, and Elite Series 1 Wireless controllers, which your giftee almost certainly has at least one of. It’s normally $49.99, but Amazon has a Black Friday deal going that brings it all the way down to $18.99, so you may want to jump on it soon.

The Nintendo Switch 2 came out a year and a half ago, and with it came what’s effectively webcam support. However, my experience is that not a lot of people are using this feature, not because it’s a bad idea necessarily, but because they don’t want to buy the expensive bespoke webcam Nintendo is selling and don’t want to move the normal one they have on their PC over to their Switch every time. So right now, for $24.98 on Amazon ($34.99 normally) you can grab a Hori USB camera that’s licensed by Nintendo and works with the Switch 2. Actually having this set up with the Switch 2 will probably prompt more people to actually bust it out (it would certainly work on me).

If your gamer likes to sit at a desk, grab ’em a mug warmer like this Sweetfull option that’s currently $16.99, down from $19.99. It’s exactly what it sounds like, keeping the liquid warm. Great for tea, coffee, and hot cocoa drinkers who have told their families to stop buying them tea/coffee/cocoa every year because they now have too much.

It’s a little cliche, but I don’t know anyone who doesn’t think a light bar is at least a little cool. This one is inexpensive ($11.99 right now, down from $14.99), simple, and looks nice, though it’ll probably stick out of the top of the stocking a bit and give away your game.

Great for PC gamers. Comes in several colors and is $8 max when not on sale. Sounds lame, but is actually very useful. The sort of thing no one buys for themselves but is always grateful to get.

Check first, but an awful lot of people who are into video games pair that interest with a card-collecting hobby. PokÃ©mon cards are a nightmare to get nowadays, but if you can snag a pack or two from the 30th Celebration set, most PokÃ©mon card fans will be happy. Magic: The Gathering‘s Reality Fracture set is a good, safe bet for Magic fans, and the One Piece TCG is currently on a set called The Dominance of God.

Zojirushi is a great brand that makes a lot of great things, including water bottles. These are usually more expensive, but for Black Friday this blue one is down to $23.49 (other colors are also on sale under $30; I cover mine with stickers which you can do to give yours a personal touch). These things are durable and can support hot or cold bevvies, and from personal experience I can say it keeps cold water cold for hours. It’s easy to forget to drink water while engrossed in a really good game, and this bottle serves as a good reminder.

Loads of them are under $30 and they come in all sorts of colors and styles. Just make sure you’re confident in which Switch (original or Switch 2) they have, so you get them one that fits.

A Steam gift card will go over well with almost anyone who plays games on their PC because they can buy whatever game has been on their wishlist without you having to guess at it. V-bucks are a great option if you know the person plays Fortnite. You can also get cards for the digital storefronts on PlayStation,Â Xbox, or Nintendo consoles.
